summary: Erie's north-shore brick light, first lit in 1873, where keeper Andrew Shaw answered fires and wrecks for 26 years, and the 1998 transfer to the state.

light.characteristic_note: Current characteristic per Rowlett (white, 3 s on, 3 s off); LighthouseFriends describes the 1873 light as fixed white with a red flash each minute until 1882

lens.note: Original fourth-order Fresnel lens (USLHS); revolving from 1882 (LighthouseFriends); replaced by a modern beacon in 1962 (LighthouseFriends)

structures.note: 67 ft (20.5 m) square brick tower attached to the keeper's dwelling (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends). Tower raised in 1896: LighthouseFriends says 17 ft 4 in; Rowlett says 33 ft
Brick keeper's dwelling with oil room, bedrooms and cistern (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett)

staffing.note: Keeper position at the light discontinued in 1933 (LighthouseFriends); enlisted Coast Guard personnel tended the light after Huntington (LighthouseFriends)

access.note: In Presque Isle State Park; nonprofit opens the tower on set hours (Fri/Sat/Sun/Mon 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., Labor Day to 28 September; 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. in October; closed after 27 October)

facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (owner, since 1998); Presque Isle Light Station Board (nonprofit, leases and operates)

events.note: Plans begun for a light on the north shore of the peninsula, to replace Erie Land Lighthouse on the mainland (LighthouseFriends)
Congress appropriates funds for the lighthouse on 10 June 1872
Construction on the peninsula begins in September 1872; brick used instead of limestone
Light first exhibited on 12 July 1873, from the tower attached to the keeper's dwelling
Original fourth-order Fresnel lens per the USLHS record; LighthouseFriends describes a fixed white light with a red flash each minute until 1882
Revolving fourth-order Fresnel lens installed; alternating red and white flash every ten seconds (LighthouseFriends)
400-foot stone-filled jetty built to stop erosion; the Board's report says the beach built out 290 feet to the west after it
Tight board fence, 396 feet long, built to keep sand off the station
Tower raised to a focal plane of 73 ft: LighthouseFriends 17 ft 4 in; Rowlett 33 ft
Kerosene adopted as the fuel; oil house built
Tower painted white
Andrew W. Shaw, Jr., becomes keeper (roster: 1901-1927)

Keeper Shaw (Andrew Shaw, jr.) assists the tug Henry E. Gillen, stranded on a bar near the station, 13 November. The Bulletin's account (January 1916 issue) gives 13 November with no year; LighthouseFriends dates the stranding 1916. Year not resolved

Fire near the station, 8 November: Shaw prevents its spread and protects government property (Bulletin 1916 volume gives day and month only). LighthouseFriends dates Shaw's firefighting near the station to 1917. Year not resolved

Shaw furnishes food and shelter to the crew of the loop yacht that stranded near the light, 10 to 12 July (Bulletin 1917 volume). LighthouseFriends places a yacht stranding near the station two years after the tug incident (about 1918), with food, shelter and clothing for three passengers
Commissioner of Lighthouses proposes to extend the power line to Presque Isle Light Station, for a brighter flashlight
Commercial electricity reaches the lighthouse (LighthouseFriends)
Fire burns on the peninsula for several days; Shaw and Robert Allen, keeper of the Presque Isle Pierhead Lighthouse, extinguish it (Bulletin 1925)
Road to the peninsula completed; Shaw retires (LighthouseFriends); Huntington keeper 1927-1933 (roster)
8 January: Keeper Frank Huntington, his wife and son rescue two boys who fell through the ice near the station (LighthouseFriends; Bulletin index entry p.234)
Lighthouse consolidated with Presque Isle North Pierhead Lighthouse; keeper position at the light discontinued; Huntington transferred to the pierhead as first assistant (LighthouseFriends)
A modern beacon replaces the Fresnel lens atop the tower (LighthouseFriends)
NPGallery record dated 4 August 1983 (date published); the sources read give no separate listing date
Officially transferred to the Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources
Tower opened for two days during Discover Presque Isle Weekend; more than 750 people paid $2 to climb
Historic Structures Report on the lighthouse published in June 2007 (LighthouseFriends)
Rule requiring the park manager to live in the park changed; the lighthouse leased to the non-profit Presque Isle Light Station Board
Nonprofit opens the station to the public
First full season: 30,000 people toured the keeper's dwelling, 13,500 paid to climb the tower; $94,000 raised (LighthouseFriends)

keepers.name: Frank S. Huntington

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS records a fourth-order Fresnel lens in 1873 as the original optic; LighthouseFriends says the 1873 light was a fixed white with a red flash until a revolving fourth-order lens was installed in 1882. Both are kept: the lens is the same order, and the 1882 change is the characteristic.

The Bulletin's account, printed in its January 1916 issue, gives 13 November with no year, which may point to 1915. LighthouseFriends dates the stranding to 1916. Both are stated in the story; not resolved.
The Bulletin's 1916 volume gives 8 November, with no year. LighthouseFriends dates Shaw's firefighting near the station to 1917. Both stated; not resolved.
The Bulletin's 1917 volume gives 10 to 12 July 1917. LighthouseFriends places a yacht stranding near the station two years after the tug incident, about 1918. Both stated; not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Checked 2026-10-22 against: the LighthouseFriends page (ID 290); the USLHS place record (presque-isle-pa; 1873, fourth-order Fresnel, keepers as in the roster); the Light-House Board report volume labelled 1891-1892 (scan p.188, jetty and beach passage confirmed); the Commissioner of Lighthouses bound volume 1915-1922 (scan p.690, printed p.85 confirmed, 'will permit a great increase in intensity of the flashlight'); the Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1916 (PDF p.4, Gillen account and 'Andrew Shaw, jr.' confirmed, and the account sits in the January 1916 issue, issue header 'Washington, January, 1916-No. 49'; PDF p.50, 8 November fire confirmed, 'protecting Government property'); 1917 (PDF p.35, loop yacht and 'food and shelter' confirmed, '10 to 12 July'); 1925 (PDF p.27, Shaw and Allen 'rendered efficient service', and 'continued several days' confirmed); the 1924-1929 index (PDF p.14, 'Huntington, Frank, keeper Presque Isle, rescue 234' confirmed); the nonprofit hours page (Labor Day to 28 September; 2 to 26 October; closed after 27 October; last climb 4:40 pm); NPGallery 83002242 (Date Published 8/4/1983); Rowlett's Pennsylvania entry (focal plane 73 ft, 3 s on 3 s off; 67 ft tower; 1896 raise 33 ft; 1998 transfer). NRHP nomination PDF for 83002242 is not digitised in our cache (placeholder); only the NPGallery asset page was read. Conflicts left for a human look: (1) LighthouseFriends dates the lens change to 1962 and the USLHS record's automation date is 1966 (source not given); the story uses 1962 with LighthouseFriends' attribution and does not state 1966. (2) Tower raise in 1896: 17 ft 4 in (LighthouseFriends) against 33 ft (Rowlett); the story gives both. (3) Huntington's service: LighthouseFriends says both 'discontinued 1933 and transferred to the pierhead' and 'served until 1944'. (4) The Gillen stranding: the Bulletin account sits in its January 1916 issue with 13 November and no year, which may point to 1915; LighthouseFriends says 1916. Not resolved. (5) The 8 November fire: the Bulletin's 1916 volume gives the day only; LighthouseFriends dates Shaw's firefighting to 1917. Not resolved. (6) The yacht: the Bulletin's 1917 volume gives 10 to 12 July; LighthouseFriends says two years after the tug incident. Not resolved. Bulletin account of Shaw's 1917 yacht is OCR-garbled around the vessel's name; only 'loop yacht' is quoted. Robert Allen's pierhead light is a separate station; accounts naming Allen are used only for the 1925 fire. Bulletin 1935 Garraty entry refers to Presque Isle, Michigan and is not used. The index page 234 account (Huntington) was not read; only the index entry is cited. Storms, wrecks and rescues chapter is drawn from Bulletins and LighthouseFriends; no newspaper search was run for this station (budget).
